svg.title: First Take the Log Out
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 4 panels. Panel 1 (Matthew 7:3): Jesus seated on a hillside, teaching two seated disciples. Caption: "Jesus sits and teaches." Jesus says: "Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the log that is in your own eye?" Panel 2 (Luke 6:41-42): a disciple with an enormous roof beam jutting from his eye and off the edge of the panel, leaning in to reach for a tiny speck in the eye of a seated brother; the beam passes over the brother's head. Caption: "The picture He paints:". A disciple says: "Brother, let me take out the speck that is in your eye,". Panel 3 (Matthew 7:5): Jesus, in a medium shot, speaking. Caption: "Jesus says:". Jesus says: "You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye,". Panel 4 (Matthew 7:5): the beam lying on the ground; the disciple kneels close to his seated brother and reaches gently for the speck in his eye. Caption: "The beam set down." Jesus says: "and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye." The point: Let God take the log out of your own eye first: tell Him, and He forgives you. Then you will see clearly to help your friend, gently (Matthew 7:5).
svg.text: A beam in one eye, a speck in the other
Let God take the log out of your own eye first: tell Him, and He forgives
you. Then you will see clearly to help your friend, gently (Matthew 7:5).
Panel 2 draws Jesus' overstatement as He says it. Each panel
names its verses; every word in a bubble is the ESV's.
